A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GP-UCB regret analysis. Their main texts, equations, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite reformatting and revised proofs.

before.justification: Figure 1 reports an original one-dimensional GP simulation, including selected-input histograms and information-gain trajectories for GP-UCB and MVR.

after.justification: V3 retains Figure 1 and adds Appendix D simulations reporting information-gain averages and quantiles over 20 sample paths.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, the GP posterior updates, and the confidence-width rule in Equation (6) are unchanged. Both versions analyze the same GP-UCB procedure.

E1.justification: Beyond v2's one-dimensional Matérn 5/2 example, Appendix D evaluates GP-generated objectives with Matérn 7/2 and squared exponential kernels and two-dimensional input domains. Coverage remains within synthetic Bayesian optimization.

E2.justification: MVR remains the empirical comparator in Figure 1 and is used again in Appendix D. No additional comparison algorithm is evaluated; Figure 1's analytic Case I reference is also retained.

E3.justification: The new Appendix D experiments report information-gain trajectories through 500 steps, while the retained Figure 1 shows 200 steps. The information-gain metric and GP-UCB–MVR comparison procedure remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix D extends the single-path illustration into an analysis of whether the information-gain gap persists across sampled objectives. Its quantile curves examine variability in this mechanism across sample paths.

E5.justification: V2 provides no repeated-run uncertainty summary for Figure 1. V3 introduces systematic reporting over 20 sample paths generated by changing the random seed, with one-standard-error bands and 10%, 25%, 50%, 75%, and 90% quantiles.

E6.justification: Figures 2–3 add average and quantile information-gain trajectories across six kernel/domain combinations, substantially expanding the empirical evidence beyond Figure 1. They report consistently lower information gain for GP-UCB than MVR across these settings; the original Figure 1 results are retained.

T1.justification: V3 replaces Lemma 2's invalid general linear condition at boundary maxima with a quadratic condition covering boundary and interior maxima. Lemmas 4 and 20 and the dependent proofs in Appendices A and C are revised accordingly. This substantively corrects the proof's foundation while preserving Theorem 3's regret rates and smoothness threshold.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same improved high-probability GP-UCB regret claims for squared exponential and sufficiently smooth Matérn kernels. The central contribution remains an information-gain analysis exploiting concentration near the maximizer.

C2.justification: V3 explicitly cautions that hidden constants prevent interpreting the fixed-parameter bounds as improvements when dimension grows. Section 4 also discusses weaker smoothness cases and qualifies the obstacle for other algorithms as a limitation of their existing analyses.

D1.justification: Figure 2 supplies explicit simulation lengthscales: 0.1 on [0,1] and 0.25 on [0,1]^2. V2's Figure 1 does not disclose a numerical lengthscale; the new disclosures do not establish a change to that retained experiment.

R1.justification: V3 adds citations to Ghosal and Roy, Kim and Pollard, and Stein to support sample-path properties and kernel differentiability. The main positioning relative to Srinivas, Scarlett, Cai, and Janz remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and most prose are retained. V3 expands sample-path explanations and limitations, removes historical correction footnotes, adds acknowledgments and Appendix D, and updates author contact information.

P2.justification: V3 adopts NeurIPS formatting, changing the title block, typography, text width, and layout throughout, and adds two six-panel figures. Figure 1 is rescaled. Figure 2 introduces a caption error: its stated kernel order differs from the panel titles.

improvement.justification: V2's linear boundary condition fails generally in multiple dimensions; v3 explains this problem and revises the dependent proofs using quadratic growth. This addresses an important validity gap in the central theoretical argument. The repeated-sample simulations and clearer parameter-dependence limitations provide additional support and precision. These gains outweigh the limited kernel-order error in Figure 2's caption.
